mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue growth and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a technology-led market rally.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a high-inflation tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a broader economic downturn.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning, which may precede a market correction; this interaction predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 95% confidence, or the interaction does not precede a market correction in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by at least 1% for three consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and rising consumption potential, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12mo MA by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 90% confidence, or the mechanism fails during a contraction in consumer confidence.
